_comment: Per-asset cross-venue lead/lag calibration for asset-specific Gate H scoring. Generated from Pass-12 lag-scan results (commit 1c328cf). Pass-12 used 30d corpora for both assets. Re-run lag scan periodically (Pass-N+5 or after major venue/microstructure changes) and update this file.

BTC.interpretation: CB-BTC leads KR-BTC by 15 minutes for regime classification. Plateau above 60% strict spans lag +8 to +21 (14 min wide), giving the system tolerance to ~±6 min lag drift around the +15 peak. Combined with sub-minute Bybit-perp lead over CB-BTC spot, Bybit-perp leads KR-BTC spot by ~15+ min total.

ETH.interpretation: ETH cross-venue divergence is structural, not timing. Lag-scan curve is flat across the entire ±10 min range (strict varies between 33.9% and 35.2%, relaxed between 56.2% and 57.9%); no timing offset rescues the gate. CB-ETH (US institutional flow) and KR-ETH (European retail/algorithmic flow) genuinely classify the same nominal price moves with different microstructure labels — different MM populations, different aggressor profiles, different fill patterns. Gate H is NOT applicable as a hard pass criterion for ETH; per-venue Gate I findings (e.g. KR-ETH WHALE_UP fade BH q=0.029, replicated 5 consecutive passes) stand on their own merits without requiring cross-venue confirmation.
